chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Ali ibn al-Hakam from his father from Abi al-Jarud from Amr ibn Qays al-Mashriqi who said:

I entered upon Husayn (peace be upon him), along with my cousin, while he was in the palace of Banu Muqatil. We greeted him, and my cousin said to him: 'O Abu Abdillah, is this dye or is your hair turning white?' He replied: 'It is the dye, and premature graying comes to us, the Banu Hashim, quickly.' Then he turned to us and said: 'Have you come for my help?' I said: 'I am an old man, burdened with debt, with a large family, and I have goods of people in my possession, and I do not know what will happen, and I dislike losing my trust.' My cousin said the same to him.

He said to us: 'Go away, so that you do not hear my call for help, nor see my black standard. Indeed, whoever hears our call for help or sees our black standard and does not answer us and does not assist us, it will be right for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to cast him headlong into the Fire on his nose.'

key_terms.بَنِی هَاشِمٍ: The Banu Hashim (clan of the Prophet)
key_terms.سَوَاداً: Black standard (symbol of the Imam's army)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for those who hear the Imam's call for help but do not assist him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the specific obligation of *Nusrah* (helping) the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that mere presence is insufficient without active response. The Imam’s warning that failure to assist results in being cast headlong into Hellfire underscores the gravity of neglecting this duty, particularly during times of crisis. The mention of 'white hair' and 'graying' for Banu Hashim serves as a unique scholarly indicator of their distinct spiritual and temporal status.
